passage: Leela, you asked why my portfolio still doesn't exist, so let me, Kunal, be honest. The first week I picked the font. The second week I changed the font. Then I decided the site needed a slide-in animation, and then a different one, and by the end of month one I had redesigned the top banner six times. I told myself it was not ready. Two months went by like that. Meanwhile, three of my classmates had put up plain pages and got interview calls. No one has seen my projects, not one recruiter, because there is nothing to click. I was so afraid of it being ordinary that I made it invisible. I still have not published it.

qa.q: How many times had Kunal redesigned the top banner?
qa.a: Kunal had redesigned the top banner six times.

qa.q: What was Kunal afraid of, according to the account?
qa.a: Kunal was afraid of the portfolio being ordinary, so it stayed hidden and nobody could see it.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Kunal use, and why?
qa.a: Kunal could publish a plain version this week and improve it later, because a visible page can get feedback and calls while an unpublished one cannot.

qa.q: How might Leela see Kunal's situation?
qa.a: Leela asked why the portfolio does not exist, and gets an honest answer, so Leela may see a friend whose skill is fine but who is stuck on polish.

grounding: Shows perfectionism about fonts and animations delaying a portfolio launch for months so that no recruiter ever sees the work.
